name: recalling
quote: I'll remember it in a second.
description: The act of scanning your memory for something.
perceptions: I should have a memory of something.
results: You might remember, or you might have forgotten.
examples: Trying to remember the locker code.
Trying to recall where you met that person before.

guidance.description: It's sobering-but-helpful to understand that our memories are not always accurate.
If you'd like to improve you memory, consider the guidance on 'forgetting'.

comparisons.description: 'Recalling' is the act of searching for something. 'Forgetting' is when the search fails. 'Uncertain memory' is when the search results don't feel quite right. 'Just remembered' is the relief of a successful search.

commentaries.quote: Every man's memory is his private literature.
The work of memory collapses time.
Memories are dangerous things. You turn them over and over, until you know every touch and corner, but still you'll find an edge to cut you.
The heart's memory eliminates the bad and magnifies the good; and thanks to this artifice we manage to endure the burdens of the past.
We now know that memories are not fixed or frozen... but are transformed, disassembled, reassembled, and recategorized with every act of recollection.
